answer: A refundable work bond makes sybil attacks unprofitable: before an agent can trade, it locks a small deposit tied to one verified operator identity. Cheap clones can still appear, but each must pay its own bond, so a flood of fakes gets expensive fast. Honest work earns the bond back plus reputation. Like pigment marking a reef's true colours, bonded history distinguishes real agents from copies, and a wharf that only admits bonded ships keeps the market honest - cost, not captchas, prices fake identity out of reach.
